messages.content: Argue that reading literary fiction improves empathy and social understanding. Cover exactly these three points: (1) literary fiction requires readers to inhabit perspectives of characters whose experiences differ from their own, directly training perspective-taking; (2) experimental research has demonstrated measurable short-term improvements in theory-of-mind scores following literary fiction reading; (3) the ambiguity and psychological complexity of literary fiction develops tolerance for uncertainty, which underlies real-world social competence. Do not address counterarguments. Write in continuous prose paragraphs only. Do not use bullet points, numbered lists, headers, bold text, or any other formatting.

message.content:
Reading literary fiction enhances empathy and social understanding by drawing readers into the inner lives of characters whose backgrounds, motivations, and circumstances often diverge sharply from their own. This immersion compels individuals to adopt and sustain alternative viewpoints throughout the narrative, thereby exercising and strengthening the capacity for perspective-taking as a core element of empathetic engagement with others in daily life. 

Experimental research has further established that exposure to literary fiction produces measurable short-term gains in theory-of-mind performance, with participants showing improved accuracy on tasks that require inferring mental states after reading such works relative to other genres or control conditions. These findings indicate that the cognitive processes involved in following complex fictional minds yield immediate, detectable enhancements in social cognition. 

The ambiguity and layered psychological detail characteristic of literary fiction also cultivate a greater tolerance for uncertainty, allowing readers to navigate unresolved motivations and shifting emotional landscapes without premature closure. This capacity for sustained openness directly supports real-world social competence by equipping individuals to handle the inherent unpredictability of interpersonal dynamics with greater flexibility and insight.
